summary: NGS survey mark for a steel lookout tower about 125 ft high, seven miles NE of Grayling; described 1949. No build date, staffing or fate found.

facts.design: Four-legged steel tower, about 125 feet high, painted black and white, with an enclosed cab at the top

events.note: First survey observation of the station. The datasheet gives no construction date for the tower.
Coast and Geodetic Survey described the station and its tower, and recorded the mark in good condition.

notes_for_editor: Only NGS datasheets describe this tower. Two searches for a Crawford County tower history found nothing on its construction, staffing or fate. The brief's agency value was the datasheet itself, so it is corrected to unknown. The brief's 38.1 m matches the datasheet's 125 feet. The story is short because the evidence is thin; a Grayling-area historical record (Crawford County Historical Society, Crawford Avalanche microfilm) could add a build date. Fact-check 2026-10-21: the 1949 sentence was reworded away from the datasheet wording, the survey point sentence now says it was the center of the base, and the story now gives metres after feet.
